name: ask_user
description: Ask the user a question through wisp and wait for their answer. Use when a decision would change the rest of your work (ambiguous requirements, risky/destructive steps, choosing between approaches). The user may take minutes or hours to answer. Do not use it for trivial choices you can make yourself.

question.description: The question, one or two sentences.

context.description: Optional markdown: what you found so far and why you are asking.

options.description: Optional suggested answers (2–4). The user can always type their own.

name: resume_later
description: Schedule a follow-up to this same task: at that time wisp sends your message back to you in this conversation, with your full context, as if the user had typed it. Use it when you must wait before you can go on (a deploy rolling out, CI running, a rate limit, "check again in 10 minutes"), or when the user asks you to do something later ("in 5 minutes do X"). After scheduling, end your turn with your report saying what you will check then; do not sleep or poll. Pass cancel with an id to drop one you scheduled.

at.description: Or an ISO time with its offset, e.g. 2026-10-25T14:30+02:00.

message.description: What to do then, written to yourself: the check to run and what to do with the result.

cancel.description: The id of a follow-up you scheduled, to cancel it instead.

name: wisp_tag
description: Tag this task with the topics it is about, so the user can find it later by searching wisp (⌘K, or #tag). Call it once you know what the task is about, in your first turn, and again only if the work moves to another topic: it replaces the tags. 3–8 short lowercase words or hyphenated terms a person would search for: the area or feature (auth, billing, search), the tech (redis, react, postgres), the kind of work (bugfix, refactor, research, release). Not the project name or words already in the title.

name: wisp_pr
description: Attach a GitHub pull request to this task, so the user sees it on the task like one opened with Ship it: its state, checks and reviews, kept current, with Merge. Call it for every PR you open (gh pr create) or work on in this task, one call per PR; a task can have several. remove=true detaches one.

pr.description: The PR’s URL (https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123), or its number in this task’s repo.

remove.description: Detach this PR from the task instead.

name: wisp_watch
description: Let the user watch your work while you do it, instead of waiting for your answer: put up a page beside this task in wisp and keep it current as you go. Worth it for long or many-step work the user would like to follow (a migration across many files, a test or benchmark run, a crawl, a data job, a design taking shape); not for quick tasks or plain questions. You decide what the page shows and how: a progress bar and a checklist, a table filling in, a chart, a diagram growing. Two ways: a page you write that draws your progress, or the real thing running (the app you are building, on its dev server). action "open": html (one self-contained page: inline CSS and JS; scripts, styles and fonts from https CDNs are fine; no fetch, no relative files), path (an .html file you wrote, read again on "reload"), or url (a running app, e.g. http://localhost:5173: start its dev server first, in the background), a title, and optionally run: { command, cwd, note }, how the user runs or checks the thing themselves (shown under the page). The page uses wisp's theme as CSS variables (var(--ink), var(--muted), var(--line), var(--accent), var(--good), var(--bad), var(--surface), var(--sans), var(--mono)) and gets your data with wisp.on('state', (s) => draw(s)) (called with the last state at once, then on every update; wisp.state is the last one). action "state": state (JSON, up to 64 KB: what the page draws now; merge: true merges it into the last one), caption optional. Send it after each meaningful step, not on every keystroke. action "caption": one line on what you are doing now. With a url: action "navigate" with path ("/settings") or url shows the page you just changed; "reload" when hot reload missed it; "state" is for your own page only. action "reload": after you edited the page. action "close": when the work is done (the page stays, with its last state; a url keeps showing while its server runs).

title.description: open: a few words, e.g. "TypeScript migration".

path.description: open: or an .html file you wrote: absolute, or relative to your working directory. navigate: the path to show, e.g. "/settings".

url.description: open: or a running app to show, e.g. "http://localhost:5173". navigate: a full url to show instead of a path.

state.description: open / state: the data the page draws, any JSON.

merge.description: state: merge into the last state (top-level keys) instead of replacing it.

caption.description: What you are doing now, one line: "Converting auth/ (12 of 40)".

run.description: open / reload: how the user can run or check it themselves, e.g. { "command": "npm test -- --watch", "cwd": ".", "note": "re-runs on save" }.

name: wisp_save
description: Save something to the user's My Stuff in wisp: their shelf of things kept from tasks (pictures, videos, documents, code, any file, links), where they browse and search them later. wisp keeps a copy, so it stays when the task or its folder goes. Call it when the user asks you to save or keep something for them ("save that to my stuff", "keep the logo"), not on your own for everything you make. One item per call; give exactly one of path, text, url or app. For a bigger thing (slides, a demo, a small tool), build it as a static web app (index.html with its JS, CSS and assets; no server, no install step; bundle dependencies in or load them from a CDN) and save its folder as app: wisp serves and launches it for the user. With id, it updates an item they already have (a mentioned one, or from wisp_stuff) instead of adding one; the version before is kept. Show what you saved in your answer as a "stuff" block with its id.

path.description: A file you made or found: absolute, or relative to your working directory.

text.description: Or text to save as a file: a note, a doc (markdown) or a snippet. Give it a name with an extension.

app.description: Or an app: a folder with index.html (or wisp-app.json naming { name, entry, description, db }). node_modules, .git, .env files, credentials, keys and source maps are left out. An app that keeps data (a demo's todos, form entries, scores) can have its own SQLite database: "db": true in wisp-app.json, or "db": "seed.sql" to make its tables (and sample rows) from that file in the app the first time. Its pages use it with import { sql } from '/_wisp/db.js'; then await sql('SELECT * FROM todos WHERE done = ?', 0) gives rows, and a write gives { changes, lastId }. One statement per call, ? for values; no ATTACH or PRAGMA. A published app has one database for everyone who opens its link: anyone with the link can read and change its data, so no personal data and no secrets in it.

cover.description: With app: a screenshot of it (png/jpg), for its card.

id.description: Update this item instead of adding one: new content (path, text, url or app) and/or title, note, tags.

name.description: File name to keep it under, e.g. "launch-plan.md". Default: the file's own name.

title.description: What the user sees on its card, a few words. Default: from the file name.

note.description: Optional: one or two sentences on what it is, to find it by later.

tags.description: Optional: 1–5 short words to find it by, e.g. ["logo", "brand"].

pin.description: With an app, in a Make a pane task only (ignored elsewhere): show it as a pane on home, or beside tasks. Pinning grants nothing: the user allows what it uses from its bar.

publish.description: With an app (new, or id alone to act on one they have): true puts it on the user's wisp Grid at a public link anyone can open (no sign-in), or updates the link it has with this version; the answer gives the link: send it to the user. false takes the link down. A key or token in its files stops the publish: the answer says which file and line; take it out and publish again. Only when the user asks to publish, deploy, host or share it. Needs them signed in to a wisp Grid (Settings → Cloud), or running in their cloud wisp.

name: wisp_stuff
description: List or search the user's My Stuff in wisp: what they (or agents) saved from tasks, newest first, each with its title, kind, note, tags and the path of its file (or its url). Read-only. Use it when the user refers to something they saved ("use the logo from my stuff"): read or copy the file from its path.

query.description: Only items whose title, name, note, tags or task have all these words.

id.description: One item in full: a doc's or snippet's text, an app's files, and how to update it.

name: wisp_blocks
description: The fields of answer blocks your instructions only name (graph, app), with an example. Read one before you put it in your final message. Read-only and answered at once.

name: wisp_stats
description: Read-only stats about the user's past wisp tasks: how many tool calls each kind of action made (run = shell, read, edit, search, web, agent, tool = other MCP tools, ask), broken down by harness, project and day, plus turns, cost, tokens and success rate. Use when the user asks about their wisp usage, which tools or harnesses their tasks use, or what tasks cost.

agent.description: Only this harness, e.g. claude, codex, opencode.

project.description: Only this project (name or id); "current" = the project of this task.

name: wisp_sessions
description: List the user's other wisp tasks, newest first: id, title, state (running | waiting | review | done), harness, project, last update and a one-line summary. Read-only. Use it to find a task the user refers to; read one with wisp_session.

query.description: Only tasks whose title or summary has all these words.

project.description: Only this project (name or id); "current" = the project of this task.

name: wisp_session
description: Read another wisp task by id: its title, state, harness, folder and branch, every request the user made in it, and a turn's report as markdown (summary, diffs, tests, next steps). Read-only. Use it when the prompt mentions a wisp task ("@Title (wisp task <id>)") or the user asks what another task did.

turn.description: Which turn's report, 1 = first. Default: the latest.

name: wisp_crew
description: List the user's crew in wisp: their long-lived agents, each with a name, role, brief, folder, harness, schedule and jobs. Read-only. Use it before changing a member, or when the user asks who is on their crew. With `member`: that one in full, their whole brief, notebook and kit (skills and instructions files, with their text), to read before you change their notebook or propose kit files.

member.description: Their name, @handle or id: read that member in full.

name: wisp_crew_add
description: Add a member to the user's crew in wisp, when the user asks for one ("add a crew member who watches CI"), or when you need help for a job and the user's brief lets you hire it. They work as tasks: on their schedule (cron), when the user tags @Name in a prompt, or when another task delegates to them. Write the brief to them, from what the user asked. Pick a short, friendly name if the user gave none. Returns the new member. When the user gives a shared crew file or link ("add the member from gist:abc123"), pass it as `from` instead.

name.description: Up to 24 letters, digits, spaces, dots, dashes or underscores; unique. The user tags them as @Name.

role.description: A few words, e.g. "CI watcher", "Docs writer".

brief.description: Their standing job and how the user likes it done, written to them ("Watch CI on main; when a run fails, find why and…"). Every job they run reads it.

cwd.description: Absolute path of the folder they work in. Default when adding: the current project. "" = no folder.

agent.description: Harness: auto, claude, codex, opencode, cursor, antigravity, grok or copilot. Default auto.

model.description: Model id for that harness; "" for its default.

effort.description: Thinking level, e.g. low | medium | high; "" for the default.

mode.description: plan = read-only, edits = auto-accept edits, auto = no permission prompts. Default auto.

cron.description: When they check in on their own, in words ("every monday", "8am every weekday", "every 30 min") or a 5-field cron, local time. "" = only when given work.

parallel.description: Jobs at once; more wait in their queue. Default 2.

paused.description: Paused members skip check-ins; work for them waits.

avatar.description: An emoji. Default: one rolled from the name.

checkin.description: Start their first check-in right away. Default false.

from.description: Instead of the fields above: members someone shared, as a link to a .crew.json file (https, or gist:<id>) or its JSON. They join paused, in cwd (default: the current project), until the user resumes them.

name: wisp_crew_edit
description: Change a member of the user's crew in wisp (rename, new brief, schedule, folder, harness, pause, notebook…) when the user asks. Only the fields given change. Their skills and instructions files aren't set here: propose those with wisp_crew_kit.

name.description: Up to 24 letters, digits, spaces, dots, dashes or underscores; unique. The user tags them as @Name.

role.description: A few words, e.g. "CI watcher", "Docs writer".

brief.description: Their standing job and how the user likes it done, written to them ("Watch CI on main; when a run fails, find why and…"). Every job they run reads it.

cwd.description: Absolute path of the folder they work in. Default when adding: the current project. "" = no folder.

agent.description: Harness: auto, claude, codex, opencode, cursor, antigravity, grok or copilot. Default auto.

model.description: Model id for that harness; "" for its default.

effort.description: Thinking level, e.g. low | medium | high; "" for the default.

mode.description: plan = read-only, edits = auto-accept edits, auto = no permission prompts. Default auto.

cron.description: When they check in on their own, in words ("every monday", "8am every weekday", "every 30 min") or a 5-field cron, local time. "" = only when given work.

parallel.description: Jobs at once; more wait in their queue. Default 2.

paused.description: Paused members skip check-ins; work for them waits.

avatar.description: An emoji. Default: one rolled from the name.

notebook.description: Their whole notebook rewritten (markdown): lasting facts and the state they compare against next time. "" empties it. To add a few lines, use remember.

remember.description: Lines to add to the end of their notebook, e.g. a preference of the user's for this job.

name: wisp_crew_kit
description: Propose skills or instructions files for a crew member's kit, when the user asks you to give them, write or improve one ("give Gucci a skill for UI reviews"). A skill is a how-to for one kind of work, read when a job fits its description; an instructions file (rules, e.g. AGENTS.md) is followed on every job. Nothing changes yet: wisp shows the files under your answer, and the user reads them and picks what to add. The same name as one they have replaces it. Read the member with wisp_crew { member } first. Write each file for them: concrete steps, checklists, commands and paths, not generic advice.

kind.description: skill, or rules for an instructions file.

name.description: A skill: lowercase-with-dashes, up to 64. An instructions file: its file name, e.g. AGENTS.md.

description.description: A skill only: exactly when to use it. That is how they know to read it.

body.description: The markdown: the skill's steps, or the instructions.

name: wisp_crew_remove
description: Remove a member from the user's crew in wisp. Their brief, notebook and schedule are deleted; their jobs stay as ordinary tasks. Only when the user asked to remove that member, or a member you added for a job is done; if unsure who they meant, ask the user first. A crew member's job can't remove that member itself.

name: wisp_connectors
description: List the user's connectors in wisp: MCP servers that every task's agent gets (in Edits and Full auto), whatever the harness. Each with its URL or command and whether it works, how many tools it has, or what it needs (a sign-in, a key). Read-only.

name: wisp_connector_add
description: Add an MCP server to the user's connectors in wisp, when the user asks ("add PostHog", "connect Linear"). Remote: give its URL (for well-known services look up their official MCP URL, e.g. https://mcp.posthog.com/mcp). Local: give the command that starts it. Never pass secret values: list the names of the env vars (local) or headers (remote) it needs, and then call wisp_connector_signin, where the user signs in or types them. A local one asks the user first, since it runs a command on their computer. wisp checks it at once and says whether it works or what it needs. Tasks get it from their next turn.

name.description: Lowercase letters, digits and _, e.g. posthog. Not "wisp".

url.description: Remote: its https URL (Streamable HTTP, or an older one ending in /sse).

command.description: Local: the command line that starts it, e.g. "npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem ~/notes".

env.description: Local: names of the env vars it needs a value for, e.g. ["GITHUB_TOKEN"]. Names only.

headers.description: Remote, for servers that take an API key instead of a sign-in: header names, e.g. ["Authorization"]. Names only.

name: wisp_connector_signin
description: Show the user a card in this task to sign in to a connector (a Sign in button for servers with an account, like PostHog or Linear) or to type the keys it needs, and wait like ask_user. It ends on its own once the connector works, or when the user skips. Call it after wisp_connector_add or wisp_connectors says one needs a sign-in or keys.

why.description: One line for the card: what it is for, or where to find the key.

name: wisp_available
description: What the user has in wisp to run work on, in one read: harnesses on this computer (installed or not, models, thinking levels), their machines (other computers and cloud computers, online or not, the harnesses on each), projects, saved subagent presets, this task's own subagents and the crew. Read-only. Read it before you pick a harness, model or machine for delegate or wisp_launch.

name: wisp_launch
description: Start a new wisp task, as the user would from wisp's prompt box: its own agent, conversation and card, which the user follows and replies to on its own. Use it when the user asks you to start, kick off or hand off tasks ("start a task to…", "open a new conversation for…", "run this on my devbox"); for help with your own work, use delegate instead. Returns the new task's id at once (wait=true blocks until it finishes or asks). Show each task you start in your answer as a "task" block.

prompt.description: The task, briefed like a colleague: goal, constraints, how to verify. It cannot see your conversation.

project.description: A project by name or id (wisp_available lists them).

cwd.description: Or a folder (absolute path). Default: this task's project.

scratch.description: No project: an empty folder of its own (questions, research).

also.description: More folders the same task works in (absolute paths).

machine.description: Run it on this machine (id or name). Default: where the project is, else this computer.

mode.description: plan = read-only, edits = auto-accept edits, auto = no prompts. Default: the user's.

worktree.description: Its own git worktree (default on in git repos, except in plan mode).

subagents.description: A team the new task's agent can delegate to: [{ agent, model?, effort?, machine?, name?, use?, count? }].

preset.description: Or a saved subagent preset's id.

wait.description: Block until it finishes or asks (up to timeout_seconds).

name: wisp_task
description: Act on another wisp task, as the user would from its card. action: reply (a follow-up, or the answer when it is asking; agent, model, effort or mode switch it from then on; queue=true waits for its current run instead of interrupting), stop, done (mark it done), archive, unarchive, rename (title), or wait (block until it finishes or asks, then return its report). Only when the user asks, or for tasks you started. Find tasks with wisp_sessions.

queue.description: reply: wait for its current run instead of interrupting it.

name: approve
description: Internal: wisp asks the user to approve a tool call your permissions do not allow on their own. Never call this yourself.

name: delegate
description:
Hand tasks to your subagents (separate coding agents the user picked, each on its own harness and model). Tasks in one call run in parallel in your working folder. By default the call waits until every task finishes and returns each report plus the files it changed; wait=false returns delegation ids at once. Delegating to a subagent again continues its conversation. A task can name a subagent of the team, or create one on the fly: agent (a harness), with model, effort and machine (to run it on one of the user's machines; wisp_available lists harnesses and machines) and a name; pass that name again to continue it. Create them when the user asks for subagents ("have codex review it", "run the tests on my devbox") or when parallel work on other harnesses pays off. A subagent on another machine gets a copy of your folder (wisp carries it: no commit or push needed): name files by their path in the folder, not absolute paths, and paste in what stays behind (git-ignored files, files outside the folder).

No team yet.

agent.description: Or a new subagent on this harness (auto: wisp picks harness and model).

model.description: With agent: its model id. Default: the harness default.

effort.description: With agent: thinking level, e.g. low | medium | high.

machine.description: With agent: run it on this machine (id or name from wisp_available). Default: this computer.

name.description: With agent: a short name for it ("reviewer"). Pass the same name later to continue that subagent.

use.description: With agent: what it is for, shown to the user.

prompt.description: The task, briefed like a colleague: goal, files, constraints, how to verify. It cannot see your conversation.

wait.description: Wait for all tasks to finish (default true).

name: subagent_results
description: Wait for delegated tasks and return their reports. Pass the ids delegate returned; with none, every task delegated in this turn.

wait.description: Default true; false returns current status at once.

name: wisp_spells
description: The spells the user has (on or off), each as its full JSON with a plain-words summary. Read-only.

name: wisp_spell_schema
description: The complete reference for writing a spell: fields, slots, parts, props, style properties, tokens, icons, actions, data sources and worked examples.

name: wisp_spell_data
description: Run a spell data source and return a sample of its real answer, so script reads the right shape. Read-only (wisp GET routes from the allowlist, read-only gh commands).

task.description: Optional task id, to fill {field} templates in gh args from that task (e.g. {pr.number}).

name: wisp_spell_check
description: Validate a spell without installing it. Returns ok and what it does in plain words, or every problem to fix. The script is compiled, never run.
